standfirst: Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg intends to maintain control over the company he founded in 2004 and a new class of stock will help him do just that.
body_markdown:
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg intends to maintain control over the company he founded in 2004 and a new class of stock will help him do just that. On Wednesday as Meta released third quarter earnings results, the company announced that it would issue a new share class of Class C stock. The share class, which is technically a one-for-one stock dividend of new Class C shares, will be distributed to all shareholders. (Fortune)

**Business Insider** adds: Meta wants to continue its "founder-led model" — so it's creating a new stock class. Bloomberg/Getty Images Meta established a new class of stock to ensure Mark Zuckerberg stayed as CEO.

**MyJoyOnline** adds: Meta Platforms has struck a deal with Mark Zuckerberg to keep him in California after the CEO warned he was considering leaving the state that houses the company’s headquarters if voters pass a wealth tax proposal next month. Under the deal, Zuckerberg will receive non-voting shares he can sell to potentially cover a multi-billion-dollar tax bill if the proposal passes, in exchange for committing to remain a resident of California, or wherever Meta maintains its headquarters, for eight years, Meta said on Wednesday.

**Financial Times Home** adds: Group to create new class of non-voting shares to allow stock sales without diluting founder’s control
